description: High-resolution optical basemap imagery pulled to visually inspect the two vulnerability-grid hotspots, as a cheap alternative to chasing SAR resolution enhancement (blocked -- see despeckle_experiment_results.json and project chat history for why). Research/internal use only, per team decision -- not for redistribution.
source: Esri World Imagery (server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery), public tile service
usage_note: Esri World Imagery carries its own terms of use (viewing/analysis permitted, redistribution restricted). Kept here for internal reference only, consistent with team decision on 2026-08-30 not to redistribute.

images.finding: Directly visible: the Odaw River channel (canalized, dark waterway) running close to the interchange, with dense informal settlement built up to its banks -- visual confirmation of the 'drainage-channel encroachment' hypothesis behind Circle's recurring flood history.

Correction to an earlier hypothesis in this project: the dark water feature here is man-made infrastructure (rectangular basins, likely a water treatment/settling facility tied to the Weija supply system), NOT a natural wetland/floodplain. This means the SAR-derived vulnerability score for this cell is likely picking up permanent infrastructure water, not transient flood risk -- worth a human sanity-check before trusting this cell's score the same way as Circle's.
